text:
Jamie R: heads-up — AcmePayments reported ~40 users unexpectedly removed from app access after their Okta bulk group update overnight. customer says they only renamed groups (dot vs dash), no intention to remove people. ticket 12345. attaching their Okta webhook payloads and our provisioning logs below. :wave:

Alex C: hmm that sounds like externalId normalization again. do we normalize dots -> dashes anywhere in the mapper? :thinking_face:

Priya S: sending repro steps i'm using locally. the customer said groups are keyed by `externalId` in their SCIM mapping. they renamed `Team.Sales.EU` -> `Team-Sales-EU` at source. our mapping uses exact match, and we also have a legacy normalization step in the group-mapper.

provisioning-bot: Received provisioning webhook from okta for org: acme-payments at 2026-03-12T03:12:14Z. batch_id=okta-20260312-004. ops=PATCH. status=processing.

Alex C: paste of the relevant log snippet from the failed run: 
```
2026-03-12T03:12:15.214Z WARN group-mapper: externalId normalization mismatch; incoming='Team.Sales.EU' normalized='team.sales.eu' mapper-key='team-sales-eu' -> no match
2026-03-12T03:12:15.215Z INFO scim: removing 40 users from role 'sales-eu' groupId=gid-42 (origin=okta-20260312-004)
2026-03-12T03:12:15.216Z ERROR provisioning: partial-success (40 removed, 0 added) commit_id=proc-89ef
```

Priya S: thanks. reproduction steps I used: 1) create group with externalId `Team.Sales.EU` in Okta 2) patch group name -> `Team-Sales-EU` 3) trigger SCIM PATCH with members unchanged 4) our service ran group-mapper and matched old normalized key but not new one -> downstream rule removed members.

Priya S: quick diagnostic curl I ran against our staging mapping endpoint: 
```
curl -X POST "$PROV_HOST/_internal/mapper/normalize" -d '{"externalId":"Team.Sales.EU"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"
# -> {"normalized":"team.sales.eu","key":"team-sales-eu"}
```

Alex C: root cause summary: we have two normalization codepaths: one used by the incoming webhook normalizer (dot-preserving -> lower/trim) and one used by the role mapping indexer (dots -> dashes). when customer renames from dot->dash, the indexer thinks it's a different logical group and issues removals.

eng-oncall: that's pretty high severity for an org with enterprise seats. what are the quick mitigations? can we make matching tolerant (dots <-> dash) at read time?

Marta K: I pushed a small tolerant-match shim to staging 15m ago. it does three things: 1) attempts exact match on externalId 2) attempts normalized match (lower/trim) 3) attempts alternate separators (dots<->dashes and underscores) and picks the best candidate. added metrics so we can see how many fall into fallback. example patch: 
```
# pseudo
match_candidates = [exact, normalize(externalId), normalize(replace(externalId, '.', '-')), normalize(replace(externalId, '-', '.'))]
choose_first_match(match_candidates)
```

Marta K: rolled to prod in canary (10% hosts) — config flag `mapper.tolerant_separators=true`. will monitor.

Jamie R: customer on the call right now — they're asking if we can re-add the removed users without them having to re-provision from Okta. any way to restore previous membership?

Alex C: yes we have a snapshot of group memberships per batch. run: 
```
# restore command (ops only)
POST /_internal/provisioning/restore
{ "org": "acme-payments", "batch_id": "okta-20260312-004", "target_group": "sales-eu" }
```
I tested locally and it re-creates the membership delta we had before the patch (it does not modify users' Okta state). use with care.

Priya S: doing the restore now in staging to validate. i'll post the delta and ask Marta to keep canary on until we confirm.

provisioning-bot: Restore job queued job_id=restore-44 for org=acme-payments initiated by Priya S at 2026-03-12T03:44:00Z

Priya S: restore finished: restored 40 users to role sales-eu. logs: `restore-44 -> success (40 applied, 0 skipped)`. pinging customer to confirm. :thumbsup:

Jamie R: customer confirmed users are back. they want a postmortem and a config toggle to opt-out of tolerant matching (they prefer strict exact-match behavior).

Marta K: opened a PR to add `mapper.tolerant_separators` default=false and documented the opt-in flow in the console under Org Settings -> Provisioning. also added unit tests and an integration test that simulates dot->dash rename. PR #4521.

Alex C: follow-ups: 1) add telemetry alert rule for >5% membership churn in single batch 2) run a scan for groups with colliding normalized keys across top 500 orgs 3) outreach to impacted customers with summary and remediation steps. assigned to eng-oncall and cx-ops.

eng-oncall: taking 1+2. will run scan overnight and post results here. setting alert for churn rate now.

Jamie R: closing loop with customer later today, leaving thread open for postmortem notes and timeline. thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :sparkles:
